headline: Ubiquitous
sub: (adj.) present everywhere. 'Smartphones are now ubiquitous in classrooms.' Use it to sound fluent.
subject: English

headline: Eloquent
sub: (adj.) fluent, expressive speech. 'The principal gave an eloquent speech on education.' Impress teachers!
subject: English

headline: Serendipity
sub: (n.) finding something good by luck. 'Discovering that book was pure serendipity.' Love this word.
subject: English

headline: Ameliorate
sub: (v.) to improve, make better. 'Good sleep can ameliorate exam anxiety.' Use in essays.
subject: English

headline: Pragmatic
sub: (adj.) practical, realistic. 'A pragmatic approach to solving problems works best.' Very useful word.
subject: English

headline: Ephemeral
sub: (adj.) lasting a short time. 'Youth is ephemeral; use it wisely.' Sounds sophisticated!
subject: English

headline: Candid
sub: (adj.) honest, frank. 'Be candid in your answers during interviews.' Shows maturity.
subject: English

headline: Meticulous
sub: (adj.) very careful, detailed. 'Meticulous revision ensures better marks.' Teachers love this.
subject: English

headline: Benevolent
sub: (adj.) kind, generous. 'A benevolent teacher helps all students.' Positive vibes!
subject: English

headline: Monotonous
sub: (adj.) boring, repetitive. 'Monotonous classes make learning harder.' Relatable for students!
subject: English

headline: Diligent
sub: (adj.) hardworking, persistent. 'Diligent students succeed in exams.' Motivation boost!
subject: English

headline: Obscure
sub: (adj.) unclear, hard to understand. 'The teacher's obscure explanation confused us.' Real talk.
subject: English

headline: Ambiguous
sub: (adj.) unclear meaning, two interpretations. 'Avoid ambiguous sentences in essays.' Grammar hack!
subject: English

headline: Tenacious
sub: (adj.) determined, persistent. 'Tenacious effort pays off in JEE prep.' Stay strong!
subject: English

headline: Vindicate
sub: (v.) prove right, justify. 'Hard work vindicates your dreams.' Inspiring reminder!
subject: English

headline: Break a leg
sub: Idiom: wish someone good luck. 'Break a leg on your exam!' NOT literal. Indian exams loved.
subject: English

headline: Piece of cake
sub: Idiom: something easy. 'This math problem is a piece of cake!' Use when confident.
subject: English

headline: Get your act together
sub: Idiom: organize yourself, improve. 'You need to get your act together for finals.' Motivational.
subject: English

headline: Hit the books
sub: Idiom: start studying hard. 'Time to hit the books for JEE!' Every student knows this.
subject: English

headline: Burning the midnight oil
sub: Idiom: working late, studying hard. 'Burning the midnight oil before exams.' So relatable!
subject: English

headline: Under the weather
sub: Idiom: feeling sick. 'I'm under the weather, can't study today.' Practical phrase.
subject: English

headline: Calling it a day
sub: Idiom: stop working, go rest. 'Let's call it a day and relax.' Perfect for study breaks.
subject: English

headline: Its vs It's
sub: It's = it is. Its = belongs to it. 'The dog wagged its tail.' Never write it's for possession.
subject: English

headline: Your vs You're
sub: You're = you are. Your = belongs to you. 'You're smart; your effort shows.' Check before submitting!
subject: English

headline: Fewer vs Less
sub: Fewer = countable (fewer students). Less = uncountable (less time). Most Indians mix this up!
subject: English

headline: Which vs That
sub: That = essential info. Which = extra info + comma. 'The exam that I failed was hard.' With comma: 'The exam, which was hard, I failed.'
subject: English

headline: Subject-Verb Agreement
sub: Plural subject = plural verb. 'The students are studying.' NOT 'students is.' Easy mistake!
subject: English

headline: Active vs Passive Voice
sub: Active: 'I solved the problem.' Passive: 'The problem was solved by me.' Use active in essays!
subject: English

headline: Apostrophe Rule
sub: Possessive: add 's. 'John's book', 'students' notes'. Plural with s: just add apostrophe.
subject: English

headline: Comma Splice
sub: DON'T: 'I studied, I scored well.' DO: 'I studied; I scored well.' OR use 'and' between clauses.
subject: English

headline: Using 'To' vs 'Too'
sub: 'To' = direction/infinitive. 'Too' = also/excess. 'You're too smart to fail.' Check this!
subject: English

headline: Pronunciation: August
sub: Say AW-gust (rhymes with 'taught'), NOT 'og-ust'. Indians often get this wrong. Practice!
subject: English

headline: Article Rule: A vs An
sub: 'A' before consonant sound, 'an' before vowel sound. 'A university', 'an honor'. Tricky!
subject: English

headline: Preposition: In vs On vs At
sub: In = place/month. On = date/surface. At = specific time/place. 'On June 25, in Delhi, at 9 AM.'
subject: English

headline: Past Tense Rule
sub: Regular: add -ed. Irregular: study the list (went, saw, was). Check before answering English papers!
subject: English
